candidates.title: Flag invoice mismatches for review

demandEvidence.chore: Identify when an invoice PDF is missing a signature or its total differs from the order amount.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: The PDF does not contain your signature

experimentPlan.output: A review queue marking supplied invoice examples as missing-signature, amount-mismatch, or needs-human-check.
experimentPlan.trigger: A shop operator supplies a sample invoice and matching order amount for review.
steps: Read only fictional or operator-supplied invoice text and order amount.
Check whether the required-signature marker is present.
Compare the stated invoice total with the supplied order amount.
Label a mismatch or uncertain extraction for review.
Show the source values beside the proposed label.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a small hand-labeled synthetic set, each label must match the known signature marker and arithmetic comparison; uncertain text must be sent to review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies permissible test inputs, defines required fields, checks every flagged case, and decides whether to contact a customer.
unverified: PDF text extraction is not supported by supplied implementation evidence.
Invoice totals may be formatted or obscured in ways the prototype cannot parse.
No source establishes how often shops encounter these cases or willingness to pay.

ease.reason: A synthetic text and amount comparison is a small mock, but no supplied source supports PDF extraction.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online shops might pay to catch invoice exceptions; this Show HN example proves neither demand nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can compare supplied text and amounts, while real PDF parsing and varied invoice formats remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed labels can repeat on supplied examples, but a person must check every exception and decide customer follow-up.

evidence.reason: The source gives two concrete mismatch examples, but they come from a product description with no frequency or independent demand evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the post illustrates missing-signature and invoice-total checks, but is a maker product description, not corroborated demand; PDF parsing is unsupported.

candidates.title: Draft booking and provider updates

demandEvidence.chore: Automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can n8n help automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts?

experimentPlan.output: A review queue with a proposed booking confirmation or provider assignment message, plus a payment-status alert draft when a supplied test record changes.
inputs: Synthetic booking ID and requested service
Synthetic booking status and assigned provider label
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator adds or changes a synthetic booking row in a local test table.
steps: Read the changed synthetic booking row and its status.
Check whether the booking ID already has a processed event key.
Map confirmed or assigned status to the matching operator-written message template.
For a payment-status change, prepare an alert draft without asserting the payment is correct.
Place the drafts and any unknown status in a human review queue.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a hand-labeled synthetic set, each known status must produce only its mapped draft, a repeated event key must not create a second draft, and an unknown state must be flagged for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies lawful test records and message templates, verifies all booking and payment states, handles failed or ambiguous cases, and approves every customer-facing message.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents booking, payment or external notification integrations for this post.
The requester gives no actual field schema, event frequency, provider system or failure examples.
Duplicate protection is only a proposed mock event-key check, not verified across concurrent live events.
Willingness to pay and recurrence of this chore are unknown.

ease.reason: A synthetic booking table can test the status-to-message draft; no supplied reference supports live booking, payment or notification integrations.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small on-demand service operators might pay for fewer missed updates; this request establishes neither payment nor frequency.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can map supplied booking states to confirmation and assignment message drafts; real APIs and concurrent events remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A bounded mock can prepare repeatable alerts, but people must confirm payment state, resolve failures and approve customer messages.

evidence.reason: The retained post explicitly asks about confirmations, provider assignment, payment updates, alerts, retries and duplicate prevention; it gives no frequency or system detail.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a useful synthetic status-to-message experiment is scopeable, but the post gives no field schema or frequency, and live integrations, payment accuracy and event handling lack supplied implementation support.
